newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate slips down amid low demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate slips down amid low demand.

text.p: Weak demand for kuna funds on Thursday further lowered the average Croatian money market rate to 8.7 percent from 9.3 percent.
Total settlements reached only 20.2 million kuna, leaving a surplus of 16.8 million kuna on the supply side.

Dealers said new borrowings were made at a rate of 8 percent for call money. Higher giro-accounts had enabled commercial banks to return a lot of earlier borrowings. Insurers rolled over previous loans at a steady 8.0 percent rate.
Wednesday's overnight trade totalled a modest 4.7 million kuna, which one bank used to maintain its mandatory reserve.

The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Friday at 5.4493 from 5.4433 against the dollar and at 3.5579 from 3.5605 against the German mark. -- Zoran radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
